title: KMT2C deficiency promotes meningioma progression through H3K27ac-mediated HIPPO Pathway Inactivation

publications.title: KMT2C Loss Promotes NF2-Wildtype Meningioma Progression and Ferroptosis Sensitivity via Epigenetic Repression of Hippo Signaling.

needs_manual_review_reason: FACT-CHECK UPDATE (2026-07-10): Publication found and linked via citation-chain search (was previously unlinked with no PMID in GEO). PMID 41642951, 'KMT2C Loss Promotes NF2-Wildtype Meningioma Progression and Ferroptosis Sensitivity via Epigenetic Repression of Hippo Signaling' (Advanced Science, 2026); the published title differs from the GEO-deposited series title but authorship (Zhang L first author, Ji J last author -- this record's only two contributors), institution (Nanjing Medical University Dept of Neurosurgery, matching this record's 'Nanjing medical universuty'), and mechanism (KMT2C loss, H3K27ac/CBP-EP300, NF2/Hippo suppression, ferroptosis/TSA rescue) all match exactly; confirmed not retracted/corrected via Europe PMC. UNRESOLVED SCOPE QUESTION (previously open, RESOLVED 2026-07-11): overall_design said only 'By knockdown the expression of KMT2C in meningioma cells...' without naming a specific cell line. Fetched the paper's open-access PMC full text (PMC13067829) directly: the RNA-seq experiment underlying this GEO series is explicitly described in Figure 3 as 'RNA-seq analysis of KMT2C-WT and KMT2C-KO cells (n = 3 per group)' (3+3=6, matching this series' sample_count exactly), performed on NF2-wild-type meningioma cells with CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KMT2C knockout. The paper's methods confirm all functional/mechanistic experiments used the established immortalized meningioma cell lines IOMM-Lee and CH157MN plus patient-derived cell cultures MN-TY1, MN-WKM2, and MN-TS1 (isogenic KMT2C-WT/KO pairs) -- no primary, uncultured patient tumor tissue was sequenced. Per docs/scope.md, 'Cell line, PDX, and organoid meningioma omics data (in vitro/model systems, not patient tissue directly)' is out of scope for the core /data/ inventory and belongs in /data/adjacent/, matching the same class of error already found and corrected for GSE263122/Ben-Men-1 in this same corpus. Of the two true corresponding authors, only Ji Jing appears in this accession's live GEO Series_contributor list (which has only 'Liuchao,,Zhang' and 'Jing,,Ji'); Tu Yiming is not a GEO contributor here, so per this corpus's established sourcing convention only Ji is retained. Series-level GEO metadata verified directly against the live source; per-sample clinical/pathology fields not applicable to a cell-line experiment. RE-VERIFICATION (2026-07-12), per-sample GSM check: all 6 GSMs were fetched (GSM8995732 'Control_1' through GSM8995737 'KMT2C-KD_3') and every one carries characteristics 'tissue: cell line', 'cell line: IOMM-Lee', 'cell type: meningioma' -- i.e. the deposited GEO series is a single established meningioma cell line (IOMM-Lee), 3 Control vs 3 KMT2C-knockdown (KD) replicates, matching the overall_design's 'By knockdown the expression of KMT2C in meningioma cells'. This DIRECTLY confirms and strengthens the adjacent-scope decision (isogenic meningioma cell-line experiment, no primary patient tissue). Note the earlier paragraph's paraphrase of the paper's Figure 3 ('KMT2C-WT and KMT2C-KO cells... CRISPR/Cas9 knockout... MN-TY1/MN-WKM2/MN-TS1') describes the publication's broader panel of functional experiments; the GEO deposit GSE297610 itself is specifically the IOMM-Lee Control-vs-KMT2C-knockdown RNA-seq (KD, not the CRISPR-KO subline), which does not change the cell-line classification.
